evals.name: settings-form
evals.prompt: in the app in this folder add a settings screen for a room: its name, a longer description under it, who can get in (private, anyone with the link, everyone on the portal) and a switch for email notifications. the name can't be empty - say so under the field if it is. while it saves, nothing should be editable and the save button should look busy. half of us run dark so it has to be right there too, and it should look like it came out of docspace.
evals.expected_output: The fixture app gains a settings screen. Fields are FieldContainer with labelVisible and isVertical, holding TextInput (with type and value), Textarea given a width, and one controlled choice component whose selection lives in the app's state. The switch is ToggleButton inside an element with a height. Validation is the app's own state driving hasError plus errorMessage, on a form with noValidate. Each text field ties its caption to its control through labelFor and a matching id, and the ToggleButton carries its own label, no control is given a tabIndex, and the fields are stacked without a gap. The tree is wrapped in ThemeProvider from providers/theme (no colorTheme) and TranslationProvider from providers/translation with a Map built from locales/en/Common.json; no stylesheet is imported. Saving puts every control into isReadOnly or isDisabled and the one primary Button into isLoading. The project typechecks and builds, and check-usage.mjs reports nothing.
assertions: each field is a FieldContainer carrying `labelVisible` — the default is false, so a container given only `labelText` renders no label at all and reports nothing

the fields are stacked without a `gap` between them, or every container is given `removeMargin`, because FieldContainer's own 16px bottom margin adds to a parent's gap rather than being replaced by it
every TextInput has both `type` and `value`, and its onChange is treated as a ChangeEvent

the multi-line field is a Textarea widened through `wrapperClassName` — it has a max-width and no width of its own, and a `style` passed to it lands on its inner scroller, which is already full width, so the field stays narrow while the code reads as though it had been fixed

the access choice is one controlled component whose selection lives in the app's own state — a ComboBox with `selectedOption` updated from `onSelect`, or a RadioButtonGroup with `selected` updated from `onClick`; neither holds a selection of its own, so a component left to itself shows nothing chosen
the notification switch is a ToggleButton inside an element with an explicit height of at least 16px, since it is absolutely positioned and otherwise overlaps the row below it
no control is given `tabIndex={0}` to make it reachable — every control in the kit is in the tab order by default, and a blanket `tabIndex` is either noise or, on a listbox option, wrong

each TextInput-based field and the Textarea ties its caption to its control: `labelFor` on the FieldContainer and the same string as `id` on the control — the Textarea's `id` lands on the `<textarea>` itself — or, where a control has no visible caption, an `aria-label` on it; the ToggleButton (and a Checkbox, if any) is captioned by its own `label` prop, since `labelFor` cannot reach it. Do not credit `labelFor`/`id` on a ComboBox, RadioButtonGroup, ToggleButton or Checkbox as naming it
the invalid name shows a message through `hasError` **and** `errorMessage` on the FieldContainer; one without the other renders nothing
native validation is kept out of the way (noValidate on the form, or no `required` attribute), or the submit handler still runs — otherwise the browser blocks submit before the error state is set
while the save is in flight the controls are genuinely not editable — `isReadOnly` or `isDisabled` reaches every one of them — rather than only being dimmed or covered
the save button carries `isLoading` while the request is in flight, rather than a label swapped to 'Saving…' or a spinner of the author's own

the tree is wrapped in ThemeProvider from providers/theme and TranslationProvider from providers/translation with a translations Map built from locales/en/Common.json — not in Providers, which needs a portal url and api key
`colorTheme` is not passed to ThemeProvider, and no value is invented for it: it is the portal's accent palette, and an application of its own leaves it out
the whole-library @onlyoffice/apps-ui-kit/styles.css is not imported: each component's CSS arrives with the component, and pulling the bundle ships 727 KB of styles the app does not use

the application's own colours are declared as a light/dark pair under the `.light` and `.dark` classes ThemeProvider writes on `<body>`, or taken from the kit's own components — no colour of the application's is left unpaired, because the kit publishes no global palette variable to reach for
the project typechecks and builds as left: `tsc --noEmit` and `vite build` both succeed
node skills/ui-kit/scripts/check-usage.mjs on the project reports zero errors and zero warnings, or the answer names each remaining warning and says why it stands

evals.name: confirm-dialog
evals.prompt: in the app in this folder: when someone deletes a room we want the usual 'are you sure' box over the page - a title, one line saying it can't be undone, and two buttons of the same width where delete is the loud red one. while the delete is running the box must not be closeable, not by the cross, not by escape, not by clicking outside, and the buttons shouldn't fire twice. it needs to look like docspace.
evals.expected_output: A dialog component built on ModalDialog. It is rendered conditionally and given `visible`; Header, Body and Footer are direct children. Both footer buttons carry `scale`; the destructive one is `primary` with `--accent-button` set through its own `style`, with no wrapper element. Closing goes through `onClose`, and `isCloseable={false}` while the request is in flight; the confirm button uses `isLoading` and the cancel button `isDisabled`, with a synchronous guard closing the same-tick window. A failed delete leaves the dialog open and says what failed. Providers are mounted, the project builds, and check-usage.mjs reports nothing.
assertions: the dialog's visibility is passed as `visible` — not isVisible, isOpen or open, which the component ignores without an error
the dialog is also rendered conditionally rather than always mounted, because `visible` toggles CSS classes and mounts nothing: the body and its effects run while it is invisible
ModalDialog.Header, .Body and .Footer are direct children of ModalDialog — a slot wrapped in a fragment or a component of the author's own renders nothing and reports nothing
both footer buttons carry `scale` so they share the row evenly, and neither is wrapped in an element of the author's own, which would take it out of the flex row and size it to its content

the red is produced by overriding `--accent-button` on the destructive Button itself, through its `style` — there is no destructive variant, and setting the variable on the dialog would recolour the close cross too
closing goes through `onClose`; while the request is in flight the dialog is made uncloseable with `isCloseable={false}` rather than by removing the handler
the in-flight state is expressed with `isLoading` on the confirm button and `isDisabled` on cancel

the same-tick double fire is closed as well: the handler returns early on a flag it sets synchronously (a ref, or a guard before the first await), not on `isLoading` alone, which only takes effect after React has re-rendered
a delete that fails leaves the dialog open and tells the reader what failed, rather than closing as though it had succeeded
the red reads on the dark theme too — either it is one colour stated to hold against both backgrounds, or it is declared per theme under the class ThemeProvider writes on `<body>`
the tree is wrapped in ThemeProvider from providers/theme and TranslationProvider from providers/translation; no composite Providers, no components/theme-provider
the whole-library styles.css is not imported
the project typechecks and builds as left: `tsc --noEmit` and `vite build` both succeed
node skills/ui-kit/scripts/check-usage.mjs on the project reports zero errors and zero warnings, or the answer names each remaining warning and says why it stands

evals.name: side-panel-list
evals.prompt: in our vite app (the one in this folder, the onlyoffice bits are installed) add a 'members' button to the page. clicking it slides a panel in from the right listing the people from src/data/members.json with name, email and role, a search box at the top that filters as you type, and a close cross. while the list 'loads' (fake a second of delay) show placeholders, and if the search finds nobody say so nicely. it has to look like docspace in both light and dark
evals.expected_output: The fixture app is extended in place. The panel is Aside (or ModalDialog with displayType aside) controlled by a boolean in state passed as `visible`, closed through `onClose`, and laid out so its last rows can be reached. The list is not Rows/RowContainer/RowContent but plain rows built from kit primitives or a Table from components/table. The search is SearchInput whose onChange receives the string. RectangleSkeleton rows during the delay, EmptyView when nothing matches, and both reset when the panel is reopened. Both providers wrap the tree; the whole-library stylesheet is not imported; nothing is imported from selectors/, billing or uploader. The project builds and check-usage.mjs reports nothing.
assertions: the panel is the kit's Aside or ModalDialog with displayType aside, and its visibility is passed as `visible` — not isVisible, isOpen or open, which the component ignores without an error
closing goes through onClose and the header cross that calls it, not by unmounting the panel with a conditional render alone

the last rows of a long list can be reached, and nothing is added to force it: Aside is a flex column whose scrolling body already takes the space under the header, so a `className` making it a column again, `withoutBodyScroll` with a scroller of the app's own, or an `!important` override of the kit scroller's inline height are all unnecessary — and the middle one costs the scroller the panel would otherwise bring
the list is built from plain rows of kit primitives or from components/table, not from Row/RowContent/RowContainer, which read children by index and measure a literal element id
the search box is the kit's SearchInput and its onChange is treated as the string it receives, unlike every other kit input
the search filters without a visible delay, or `refreshTimeout` is lowered — the default debounce is a whole second
RectangleSkeleton (or Loader with an explicit type) renders during the delay; a bare Loader, which shows its label as text and no spinner, is not used
an empty result renders EmptyView or an explicit line of text, not a blank body
reopening the panel starts it clean — the fake delay runs again and the search box no longer holds the previous term

the tree is wrapped in ThemeProvider from providers/theme and TranslationProvider from providers/translation with a translations Map built from locales/en/Common.json — not in Providers, which needs a portal url and api key
the whole-library @onlyoffice/apps-ui-kit/styles.css is not imported — each component's CSS arrives with the component
no import specifier contains PUBLIC_DIR, /dist/, selectors/, billing, uploader or ai-agent

the application's own colours — the panel's rows, its empty state, its skeleton backgrounds — are declared as a light/dark pair under the `.light` and `.dark` classes ThemeProvider writes on `<body>`, with none left unpaired, because the kit publishes no global palette variable to reach for
the project typechecks and builds as left: `tsc --noEmit` and `vite build` both succeed
node skills/ui-kit/scripts/check-usage.mjs on the project reports zero errors and zero warnings, or the answer names each remaining warning and says why it stands

evals.name: explain-empty-labels
evals.prompt: we pulled the onlyoffice components into our app and some of the text is just gone. the toast we show after saving has no title, just a gap where it should be, and the three-dot menus on the cards are blank too. console says something about i18next and a missing key. the buttons we label ourselves are fine. what did we miss?
evals.expected_output: The answer names TranslationProvider from @onlyoffice/apps-ui-kit/providers/translation as the missing piece, and the shape of what it needs: a Map of language to a Map of namespace to the flat table, built from @onlyoffice/apps-ui-kit/locales/en/Common.json. It explains why only some text is missing — text passed as props is the caller's, while the toast titles and the tile menus are looked up in the Common namespace — and why the result is empty rather than the raw key: the kit's lookup returns an empty string when it can find no instance, and logs one line per key. It says that a provider given no translations installs no context at all, so mounting the element is not the fix; that the provider builds an i18next instance of its own, so the usual I18nextProvider / addResourceBundle advice does not reach the kit's labels; and that the package ships English only, in three namespaces.
assertions: names TranslationProvider from @onlyoffice/apps-ui-kit/providers/translation as what is missing
gives the shape of `translations`: a Map of language to a Map of namespace to the key/value table, not a plain object
points at @onlyoffice/apps-ui-kit/locales/en/Common.json as the table the kit's own labels come from, rather than telling the reader to write the strings themselves
says that mounting the provider is not by itself the fix: given no `translations` it installs no context at all and renders only its children, so the Map is the working part
says the provider builds an i18next instance of its own, so the usual advice — an `I18nextProvider`, or `addResourceBundle` on the application's own singleton — does not reach the kit's labels
explains why only some text is affected: labels passed as props are the caller's, while toast titles and the tile menus are looked up in the Common namespace at call time
explains that the text comes out empty rather than as the raw key because the kit's lookup returns an empty string when there is no instance
says the package ships English only, in three namespaces, and does not name locale files it does not have
does not offer the theme provider, a missing stylesheet or a bundler setting as the cause; naming one in order to rule it out is fine
every API it names exists — the provider, its `translations` and `locale` props, and the `locales/en/Common.json` table — with no invented prop, hook or i18next option

evals.name: audit-snippet
evals.prompt: someone left this file behind on a branch - fixtures/audit-snippet/Panel.tsx. the panel never opens and I don't trust the rest of it either. what's wrong with it?
evals.expected_output: A review naming, at minimum: `isVisible` on Aside, which the component does not read (its prop is `visible`), as the reason the panel never opens; the import from selectors/People, which is portal-internal and fetches through the DocSpace REST client, with the generic Selector named as the consumer's replacement; the PUBLIC_DIR specifier, which is a DocSpace client webpack alias that resolves nowhere else; and the whole-library styles.css import, which is unnecessary because each component imports its own CSS and costs 727 KB. It also catches the FieldContainer without labelVisible and without labelFor, the TextInput without its required type, the column gap doubling the field spacing, and the SearchInput handler reading .target.value off a string — and it says what it checked against.
assertions: names `isVisible` on Aside as the reason the panel never opens, and gives `visible` as the prop the component actually reads

states plainly that the import from selectors/ is portal-internal — it fetches through the DocSpace REST client and a portal store, so it cannot work outside the portal — without handing the check back to the reader, and names the generic `Selector` as what a consumer uses instead
names PUBLIC_DIR as a DocSpace client webpack alias that does not resolve for a consumer of the package
names the whole-library styles.css import as unnecessary, and gives the reason: each component imports its own CSS, so the import adds nothing the components do not already bring
gives the cost of that import as the whole library's stylesheet, around 727 KB the application does not use
names the SearchInput onChange handler reading `.target.value`, since that callback receives the string itself
names the FieldContainer without `labelVisible`, whose default is false, so the label is not rendered

names that the field's caption is attached to nothing: there is no `labelFor` on the container and no `id` on the input, so even once `labelVisible` is added the label would caption nothing and the field would still be announced unnamed
names the TextInput missing its required `type`
names the column `gap` doubling the spacing against FieldContainer's own 16px bottom margin, which adds to a gap rather than collapsing into it
does not treat the styles.css import as necessary: it is not defended, kept or repaired, and no stylesheet import is recommended in its place
at most one finding cannot be pointed at a line of the file, and the review does not frame the file as a DocSpace plugin — nothing in the prompt says it is one, and the advice differs
says what it checked the file against — the kit version it read, and what it could not read — rather than presenting library facts with no source

evals.name: explain-aside-prop
evals.prompt: quick one before we start - we're about to put a side panel in our app with the onlyoffice ui kit, nothing installed here yet. what's the prop that opens Aside, and is it the same one on ModalDialog and Tooltip? and tell me where you got that from, i don't want a guess
evals.expected_output: The answer says Aside opens with `visible`, that ModalDialog reads the same prop, and that Tooltip is different: `isOpen`. It says there is no single name across the kit and that a wrong one is ignored with nothing logged, so `isVisible` opens nothing. It names where it read this — the component's page on the docs site (https://api.onlyoffice.com/docspace/ui-kit/ui/overlays/aside.md and the pages beside it) or the component's README inside the installed package — rather than answering from memory, and it does not build anything.
assertions: names `visible` as the prop that opens Aside
says ModalDialog reads `visible` too, and Tooltip reads `isOpen`, so the name is per component
says a wrong prop name is ignored silently — nothing is logged, the panel never appears
does not offer `isVisible`, `open` or `opened` as Aside's prop
names its source: the component's page on the docs site under docspace/ui-kit, or the README inside the installed package — not memory
answers the question instead of scaffolding a project or asking for one

evals.name: explain-loader-vs-skeleton
evals.prompt: building a list screen with the onlyoffice apps ui kit, no project yet, just planning. while the rows are loading should i show Loader or RectangleSkeleton? someone said Loader sometimes renders text instead of a spinner, is that real? point me at the page you read
evals.expected_output: The answer picks RectangleSkeleton for a list whose shape is known — placeholders in the shape of the rows, so the layout does not jump — and reserves Loader for a wait of unknown duration with nothing to stand in for. It confirms the Loader behaviour: without an explicit `type` (`LoaderTypes.oval`, `dualRing`, `track`, …) it renders its label as text and no spinner. It warns that the skeletons are fixed-colour and should be looked at in the dark theme. It points at the pages it read — the docs site's skeleton and loader pages under docspace/ui-kit/ui/ (`ui/skeletons/rectangle`, `ui/status-components/loader`), found through llms.txt, or the READMEs inside the package — and names them.
assertions: recommends RectangleSkeleton for a loading list and gives the reason: the placeholders have the shape of what is coming, so the layout does not jump
reserves Loader for a wait with no known shape or duration, rather than treating the two as interchangeable
confirms that Loader without an explicit `type` renders its label as text and no spinner
names at least one real `type` value, such as `LoaderTypes.oval`, `dualRing` or `track`
mentions that the skeletons are fixed-colour and worth checking in the dark theme
names the page it read on the docs site (a URL under api.onlyoffice.com/docspace/ui-kit/) or the README inside the installed package, rather than citing nothing
does not invent a component or a prop — no `Skeleton`, `isLoading` on a list, or `spinner` prop
